articles.title: Gauff responde tras recibir insultos racistas por un punto repetido: "No soy una tramposa"
articles.standfirst: La estadounidense, que ganó a Sun Xinran, salió al paso de los mensajes de odio después de que parara un punto, y hubiera que repetirlo, por un problema con los carteles publicitarios
articles.summary: La estadounidense, que ganó a Sun Xinran, salió al paso de los mensajes de odio después de que parara un punto, y hubiera que repetirlo, por un problema con los carteles publicitarios
articles.body: Coco Gauff, que se impuso este lunes a la tenista local de 16 años Sun Xinran por 7-5 y 6-1, respondió a las críticas racistas que recibió en redes sociales después de que hubiera que repetir un punto que ella misma paró por problemas con los luminosos de la publicidad. La estadounidense aseguró que "puede no gustarles o estar en desacuerdo con lo que pasó sin ser racistas. La cantidad de comentarios y mensajes directos racistas que he recibido en las últimas horas es increíble. Por último, no soy un tramposa ni un ladrona". Después, la tenista explicó lo ocurrido cuando en el primer set, cuando estaba sacando y el encuentro iba 5-4, con 15-15. Al final de un largo intercambio de golpes, Gauff levantó la mano para interrumpir el juego, justo antes de que Sun alcanzara una volea y enviara la pelota lejos para conseguir un punto ganador que la habría dejado a dos puntos de ganar el primer set. Justo antes de eso, mientras Sun se preparaba para golpear la pelota, las vallas publicitarias situadas en los laterales de la pista cambiaron sus anuncios y eso fue lo que llevó a Gauff, según admitió, a detener el juego. Había visto parpadear las vallas al comienzo del punto, pero "no estaba segura de si eso era lo que realmente había visto", escribió. El juez de silla realizó una revisión de vídeo y determinó que el parpadeo constituía un obstáculo, por lo que el punto se repitió.

articles.title: La liberación de Simona Halep: "Me gustaría dejar de ser un objeto de consumo público"
articles.standfirst: "Deseo y vivir libremente, sin juicios constantes, sobre todo porque han salido innumerables artículos y opiniones sobre mí, y siguen saliendo"
articles.summary: "Deseo y vivir libremente, sin juicios constantes, sobre todo porque han salido innumerables artículos y opiniones sobre mí, y siguen saliendo"
articles.body: ESimona Halep ha hablado en 'Sports Festival x 30:0' sobre su retirada del tenis en febrero de 2025 con 33 años y su nueva vida. En una entrevista titulara 'Me siento liberada' Simona Halep compartió que, tras una carrera marcada por grandes logros y una enorme exposición mediática, su deseo es construir una vida lejos de los focos junto al empresario Dorin Mateiu, 24 años mayor que ella. La trayectoria deportiva de Halep dio un giro decisivo tras el US Open de 2022, cuando fue suspendida durante cuatro años debido a un control antidopaje positivo por roxadustat, sustancia que ingirió a través de un suplemento alimenticio contaminado. Más tarde, el Tribunal de Arbitraje redujo la sanción a nueve meses, permitiéndole regresar a la competición tras 568 días de inactividad. Sin embargo, ante la imposibilidad de recuperar su antiguo nivel, optó por retirarse del tenis. "Durante muchos años pertenecí a todo el mundo y ahora ha llegado el momento de pertenecerme a mí misma. Quiero formar una familia como deseo y vivir libremente, sin juicios constantes, sobre todo porque han salido innumerables artículos y opiniones sobre mí, y siguen saliendo", declaró la exnúmero uno del mundo, que anteriormente estuvo casada con el empresario Toni Iuruc. Simona Halep (25 años) subrayó "me gustaría mucho dejar de ser un objeto de consumo público, permitirme vivir mi propia vida y hacer que la gente entienda que la deportista Simona Halep cerró su ciclo en el deporte". "Ahora seré una persona normal, como todas las demás", sentenció.

articles.title: Jannik Sinner: World number one ends season early with knee injury
articles.summary: World number one Jannik Sinner will not play again in 2026 because of an ongoing right knee injury.
articles.body:
World number one Jannik Sinner will not play again in 2026 because of an ongoing right knee injury.

The Italian has not played competitively since defending his Wimbledon title in July.

Five-time Grand Slam champion Sinner said he "needed to think about my long-term career" when deciding to end his season early.

"Me together with the doctors have decided that I need a course of treatment for my knee," the 25-year-old said in an Instagram video.

"The last couple of years gave me so many beautiful feelings and emotions, which this year is going to be way different.

"I will do everything possible to get back 100%."

Sinner was the dominant player for much of the year, winning 44 and losing just three of his singles matches.

He won five Masters 1000 titles in a row between March and May, becoming the youngest man to complete the 'career Golden Masters'.

Sinner's injury means that Alexander Zverev is all but guaranteed to replace him as world number one by the end of the year.

Second-ranked Zverev, who has won the French Open and US Open this year, trails Sinner by 1,280 points in the live rankings.

However, Sinner will be unable to defend the points he claimed with title triumphs in China, Vienna, Paris and the ATP Finals at the end of last year.

Sinner won six titles in 2026 on all three surfaces and lost just one singles match between March and July.

He reached the semi-finals of the Australian Open, losing in five sets to Novak Djokovic, but suffered a shock second-round exit at the French Open in May.

The loss to Juan Manuel Cerundolo in hot and humid Paris conditions ended Sinner's 30-match winning streak.

However, he bounced back superbly at Wimbledon. Despite being taken to five sets in the first round - and bleeding through his shoes at one point - he recovered to eventually beat Zverev in the showpiece and defend his title.

Sinner and generational rival Alcaraz, having met in three of the four Grand Slam finals last year, only played each other once in 2026.

Sinner came out on top, beating the Spaniard in the Monte Carlo Masters final to replace him as world number one.

He finishes the year with a 10-1 record against top-10 players, with his sole defeat coming against Djokovic in Melbourne at the start of the year.

articles.title: Jannik Sinner: World No 1 to miss rest of season due to knee injury and has not played since winning Wimbledon
articles.summary: Jannik Sinner will not return to the court until 2027; Italian's last match was victory over Alexander Zverev in Wimbledon final in July; five-time Grand Slam champion could lose No 1 ranking before end of season with Zverev pushing for that spot; watch tennis live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Speaking in a video message on social media, the Italian said: "Me, together with the doctors, have decided that I need a course of treatment for my knee, which means that the 2026 season is officially over.

"The last couple of years gave me so many beautiful feelings and emotions, which this year is going to be way different, but I also need to think about my long-term career so I will do everything possible to get back 100 per cent.

"I will thank you already in advance for your support and hope to see you very, very soon on court again. Ciao ciao!"

Sinner's team added in a statement: "On the advice ​of his ⁠medical team, Jannik ⁠Sinner will follow a course ‌of treatment for inflammation in his knee.

"The decision has been made to have the treatment ⁠now to give ​Jannik the necessary ​time to recover ​before beginning preparations for ⁠2027.

"As a result, Jannik will be ⁠unable to compete ​again during the 2026 ​season."

Sinner beat Alexander Zverev in the Wimbledon final in July to successfully defend his title and claim a fifth major trophy, after also winning the Australian Open in 2024 and 2025 and US Open in 2024.

He picked up six trophies in 2026, preceding his Wimbledon success with victories in the ATP 1000 events at Indian Wells, Miami, Monte Carlo, Madrid and Rome, and won 44 of his 47 matches across the year.

Sinner's only defeats came to Novak Djokovic in the Australian Open semi-finals, Jakub Mensik in the last eight in Doha and a shock loss to Juan Manuel Cerundolo in the second round of the French Open amid sapping conditions.

The 25-year-old - who has won his last 10 ATP finals - skipped the US Open and also pulled out of his China Open defence and then the upcoming Shanghai Masters.

He will now miss the Paris Masters as well as the ATP Finals and Davis Cup Finals in his homeland.

Sinner's premature end to the 2026 campaign means he could be dethroned as world No 1 before the year is over, with Zverev pushing for that ranking.

Sinner is on 11,000 points with world No 2 Zverev - knocked out in the China Open quarter-finals by Djokovic at the weekend - on 9,720.

Carlos Alcaraz, Ben Shelton and Daniil Medvedev complete the current top five.

articles.title: Alcaraz olvida la lesión en la muñeca defendiendo la corona de Tokio
articles.standfirst: El murciano, verdugo de Lehecka en dos sets, es el tercer jugador que repite título un año después
articles.summary: El murciano, verdugo de Lehecka en dos sets, es el tercer jugador que repite título un año después
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz se ha convertido este martes en el tercer jugador capaz de defender la corona de Tokio después de Stefan Edberg (1989-91) y Pete Sampras (1993-94) tras derrotar en la final de Tokio a Jiri Lehecka, por 7-6(4) y 6-4, en 1 hora y 36 minutos. Es apenas el cuarto profesional de la raqueta que llega a los 10 títulos en torneos de la categoría 500 desde su introducción en 2009. Se une a un club donde sólo estaban Novak Djokovic, Rafael Nadal y Roger Federer. Su celebración, abrazándose a todos los miembros de su banquillo, indica la importancia del éxito. Su última corona databa del 21 de febrero en Doha. Alcaraz volvió a firmar una nueva remontada en la central del Ariake Coliseum. Lehecka se adelantó con un 0-2, gracias a un break inicial. Y también dominaba 2-4 en la muerte súbita. Cinco puntos seguidos del murciano le dieron el parcial y la mitad de la final. El campeón de siete grandes se conocía la táctica a utilizar ante el checo. Por algo le había derrotado en tres de los cuatro precedentes. Una pelota fuerte, otra blanda, una alta, otra cortada... Jiri se llenaba de bola hasta fallarla. La final se terminó con la segunda rotura del fenómeno de El Palmar en el séptimo juego de la continuación. Ni el mejor partido de Lehecka le llega para inquietar al español. Carlitos se mantiene invicto en la capital japonesa: 10 partidos y otras tantas victorias. Aunque aún le queda para llegar a los 33 triunfos que presenta Djokovic en Pekín. A pesar de haberse perdido cuatro meses y medio de competición se sitúa tercero en la Race 2026, superando a Ben Shelton y quedándose por detrás de Alexander Zverev y Jannik Sinner. Las 13 veces que ha perdido el saque en los cinco partidos de Tokio quedan en el olvido por su corona y porque su nivel tenístico es de otro planeta. Olvidada la lesión en la muñeca derecha es el gran candidato a ganar todo lo que le queda: Masters 1000 de Shanghái y París, las ATP Finals, la Copa Davis y el Six Kings Slam. El sábado debutará en el cuadro individual de Shanghái con el ganador del duelo entre Juan Manuel Cerúndolo y un rival de la fase previa.

articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz, con apenas 23 años, ha conquistado este martes en Tokio el vigésimo séptimo trofeo de su carrera en el circuito profesional de la ATP. Eso le convierte en el tercer español más laureado de la Era Open, atrapando a David Ferrer, el actual seleccionador de la Copa Davis. Por delante de él ya sólo restan Rafael Nadal (92) y Manuel Orantes (34). El pupilo de Samuel López, que hace doblete en la capital nipona, tiene el honor de sumar el entorchado 470 de la Armada masculina desde 1968. Entre los jugadores en activo, sólo Novak Djokovic (101) y Jannik Sinner (30) han ganado más que Carlitos. De hecho, el título del murciano le permite desempatar con Alexander Zverev.

articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz ha conquistado este martes el tercer título de la presente temporada y el que es el vigésimo séptimo de su carrera profesional tras deshacerse de Jiri Lehecka en la final del torneo de Tokio. Alcaraz suma 500 puntos por la corona que le permiten regresar al podio de la Race 2026 adelantando a Ben Shelton y situándose por detrás de Alexander Zverev y Jannik Sinner. Los cuatro están matemáticamente clasificados para las ATP Finals de Turín (15 al 22 de noviembre) aunque el italiano ha anunciado su baja por la lesión en la rodilla derecha. Lehecka, finalista, se lleva 330 puntos. Carlitos ingresa un talón de 764.750 dólares por los 411.480 de Lehecka. La victoria le permite al murciano superar por primera vez en su carrera los 66 millones de dólares en premios.

articles.title: China Open: Daniil Medvedev finally runs out of chances with disqualification against Novak Djokovic
articles.summary: Daniil Medvedev once said you would need to knock on his hotel door at 6am for seven days in a row to make him angry - but his China Open disqualification was no surprise.
articles.body:
Daniil Medvedev once said you would need to knock on his hotel door at 6am for seven days in a row to make him angry.

On court, though, he is a far more combustible character who finally ran out of chances when he was disqualified from Monday's China Open semi-final against Novak Djokovic.

Djokovic was serving for a place in the final when the ball ricocheted off the back of the court. Medvedev swiped it into the stands, where it hit a spectator in the face.

A few minutes later the Russian was defaulted, as he had to be, under rules that bar a player from "hitting a ball dangerously or recklessly, or with negligent disregard of the consequences."

Players have got away with worse. There is sometimes anger in their actions, but it is rarely of the bulging-neck-vein variety.

It is more often a sign of irritation and petulance, with frustrations taken out on the ball with little care for the safety of officials, ball kids and the spectators who line the court.

"I can only say I'm a really calm person in life - I actually have no idea why the demons go out when I play tennis," Medvedev said at the 2019 US Open, where he was fined for snatching a towel from a ball person and making an offensive gesture to fans inside the Arthur Ashe Stadium.

"Especially when I was a junior, I had a lot of problems with my attitude.

"I was not getting defaulted, but to have a game penalty was easy."

Returning to the theme at that year's end-of-season ATP Finals, Medvedev said any bad blood soon disappears after leaving the court.

"All my temper goes away after I leave the tennis court. If I'm not happy with my practice, I step out of the court and five minutes later, I'm OK," he said.

It is hard - and probably unwise - to take your eyes off Medvedev's matches, and he is very popular with the media for his engaging, reflective and humorous interviews once the dust has settled.

But he has gone too far on court on many occasions, with much of his aggression directed at umpires.

At Wimbledon in 2017, a 21-year-old Medvedev was so incensed about some of the decisions made by umpire Mariana Alves in his second-round match that he sprinkled coins at her feet as she climbed down from the chair.

He later apologised and denied he was accusing her of bias.

Two years ago, again at Wimbledon, it appeared officials were considering defaulting Medvedev for an outburst towards umpire Eva Asderaki-Moore.

Medvedev claimed he said something in Russian which was "not pleasant, but not over the line" - and, after a discussion between the umpire, supervisor and tournament referee, he escaped with a code violation for unsportsmanlike conduct.

He was fined more than £60,000 for his behaviour at the 2025 Australian Open, which included trying to destroy a net camera, and had an infamous meltdown later that year at the US Open.

On a rowdy New York night, Benjamin Bonzi had match point for a straight-set win against Medvedev in the first round when a photographer inexplicably walked on to court between his first and second serves.

Umpire Greg Allensworth awarded the Frenchman another first serve because of the delay, sparking fury from Medvedev.

Medvedev accused Allensworth of hoping to engineer a quick finish - as he gets paid by the match, rather than the hour - and there was a pause of over five minutes as he whipped up the crowd.

He did save the match point, but went on to lose in five sets before obliterating his racquet by smashing it repeatedly against the table next to his chair.

Medvedev will lose all the prize money and ranking points he earned from his run to the semi-finals in Beijing. He remains in the eighth and final qualifying spot for November's ATP Finals, but the loss of 200 points could yet prove crucial.

The 30-year-old has apologised for his actions and said he hopes to say sorry to the spectator in person.

In New York a month ago, Medvedev reflected on the role of genetics when explaining how his eldest daughter has "my personality on the court".

"She plays a bit. She enjoys it. Maybe it's a bit of a genetic somewhere there," Medvedev added.

"I took her to practice once. She's happy, so she throws the racquet through the whole court.

"The coach looks at me and says: 'I don't know where she got this from...'

"All the people that talk about that I should control myself more - she's three years old. It's not like we taught her to do the things she's doing on the court."

articles.standfirst: El murciano ofrecía el trofeo a su equipo, que ha trabajado muy duro para que regresara en plenas condiciones
articles.summary: El murciano ofrecía el trofeo a su equipo, que ha trabajado muy duro para que regresara en plenas condiciones
articles.body: La imagen de Carlos Alcaraz celebrando a lo grande su segundo título seguido en Tokio contrastaba con la de Jiri Lehecka hundido en la silla de cambios. El fichaje de Frederic Fontang, ex de Felix Auger-Aliassime no le ha servido al checo para ganar al murciano. El último título de Alcaraz databa del 21 de febrero en el Open 500 de Doha. Luego vendría la lesión en la muñeca de Barcelona. "Ha sido un proceso lento, con dudas, pero con mi equipo hemos trabajado duro para volver estando seguros de que no me volvería a lesionar", decía el murciano en la ceremonia de premiación. "Estoy muy contento de volver a levantar un trofeo después de un tiempo. Tiene un extra de especial después de mi lesión y mi regreso. Era apenas el segundo torneo que juego y significa mucho para mí. Ha sido una semana en la que no he encontrado mi mejor nivel de tenis, pero sí he sido capaz de encontrar las soluciones adecuadas", decía el flamante campeón.

articles.title: ‘It’s been a while’: Carlos Alcaraz becomes first player since Pete Sampras to retain Japan Open
articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz completed a successful return from a lengthy injury layoff by retaining his Japan Open title on Tuesday, beating unseeded Czech Jiri
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz completed a successful return from a lengthy injury layoff by retaining his Japan Open title on Tuesday, beating unseeded Czech Jiri Lehecka 7-6(4), 6-4 in the final.The Spaniard, who endured a slow start yet again, eventually found his rhythm to claim his third title of the year and 27th overall. The ATP 500 triumph came in only his second tournament since returning from a wrist injury that kept him sidelined for nearly five months.Alcaraz made his comeback at the US Open in late August and has now quickly rediscovered his winning touch. He had earlier won the Australian Open and Qatar Open this year.Alcaraz overcomes slow start to retain titleThe world No. 3 began the final nervously, dropping his serve in the opening game, but quickly settled and raised the intensity. He broke world No. 19 Lehecka with a powerful backhand to level the first set at 3-3 and gradually took control of the contest.The Czech continued to put pressure on Alcaraz and took advantage of some uncharacteristic errors in the tiebreak, but the Spaniard responded with a sublime drop shot before closing out the opening set 7-4 in the tiebreak.Alcaraz then took control midway through the second set, breaking Lehecka to move 4-3 ahead. He completed the victory by forcing an error on match point before celebrating enthusiastically with his team courtside.The title made Alcaraz the first player since American great Pete Sampras in 1993-94 to win the Japan Open in consecutive years. More importantly, it provided another confidence boost after the uncertainty of his injury-enforced absence."I'm really happy to be able to lift a trophy again," Alcaraz said. "It's been a while and obviously it's extra special after my injury and my comeback, in the second tournament that I'm playing."It was a really tough week and I didn't play my best tennis and my best level but I did find good solutions and that's what matters in the end."‘A lot of negative thoughts come to your mind’Alcaraz admitted that his injury layoff had brought plenty of uncertainty about whether he would be able to return at his previous level. Winning a title so soon after his comeback has helped put those concerns behind him."A lot of negative thoughts come to your mind," Alcaraz added."If you're going to come back healthy, if you're going to come back the same as you were before, if I will be able to hit the ball normally without pain. I trusted myself and it worked out."The 23-year-old will now turn his attention to the Shanghai Masters, where he will face Juan Manuel Cerundolo or a qualifier in his opening match. articles.title: ‘I'm not a cheater or a thief’: Coco Gauff hits back at racist abuse after China Open controversy
articles.summary: Coco Gauff has hit back at an “insane” wave of racist abuse on social media after her controversial China Open victory over home teenager Sun Xinran on
articles.body: Coco Gauff has hit back at an “insane” wave of racist abuse on social media after her controversial China Open victory over home teenager Sun Xinran on Monday.The American, a two-time Grand Slam champion, defeated the 16-year-old 7-5, 6-1 to reach the fourth round in Beijing, but found herself targeted online after an incident late in the opening set.Gauff stopped play during a crucial rally after noticing a flickering advertising board courtside, just as Sun appeared poised to put away a winner. The chair umpire subsequently ordered the point to be replayed after a video review, and Gauff won the replay before holding serve to level the set at 5-5.Gauff responds to racist messagesThe incident triggered a backlash on social media, with Gauff saying she was subjected to a barrage of abusive messages following the match. Responding to a post containing a racial slur on X early Tuesday, the 22-year-old American made clear that criticism of her actions did not justify racist abuse.“You can dislike me or disagree about what happened without being racist,” Gauff wrote. “The amount of racist comments/direct messages I've received in the last few hours is insane.“Lastly, I'm not a cheater or a thief.”Gauff also explained that she had acted within the rules by challenging the point. Players can request video reviews for certain judgment calls, including situations in which a distraction may have interfered with play.The scale of online abuse directed at tennis players has been a growing concern for the WTA. The governing body has introduced an AI-powered system to monitor thousands of social-media posts involving players and officials. A study by the WTA and World Tennis found that players were subjected to more than 12,000 abusive posts and messages in 2025, up from around 8,000 the previous year.What happened during the controversial point?The controversy began when Gauff stopped a rally after electronic advertising boards around the court flickered during the point. Sun appeared to be on course to win the rally when Gauff raised her hand and stopped play. Following a video review, the umpire ruled that the point should be replayed. Gauff won the replayed point and then held serve to make it 5-5 before taking control of the match.Gauff said she had spoken to Sun after the contest and apologised for the situation. The Chinese teenager, who received a wildcard for the tournament and was making her WTA Tour debut, appeared emotional following the defeat. She had recently won the US Open junior title.“Xinran's an incredible talent and player, I apologised for the situation at the end of the match and she completely understood,” Gauff wrote.“I didn't like to see her so emotional as I've been there and I really understand what it's like but this is the beginning of an incredible career. It was an honour to share the court in front of her home crowd.”Gauff, who herself reached the Wimbledon fourth round as a 15-year-old in 2019, said she understood the emotions Sun was experiencing after such a high-profile match. articles.summary: El serbio, a sus 39 años, amplia su racha de partidos ganados en el torneo y establece una marca de 34-0
articles.body: Novak Djokovic tiene dos marcas que le gustaría acometer antes de colgar la raqueta: alcanzar los 25 títulos del Grand Slam y superar los 109 torneos ganados por Jimmy Connors en la Era Open. Los 102 que ya suma el serbio, tras ganar por séptima vez en Pekín, le sitúan a uno de Roger Federer. Nole estrena su palmarés en la presente temporada en su evento fetiche y ya van 21 seguidas ganando. Ha decantado a su favor los 34 partidos disputados en el China Open. Él sí que es la Gran Muralla China para los demás. Es el primer jugador que se corona por encima por encima de los 39 años desde el australiano Ken Rosewall, que tenía 43 cuando se adjudicó el triunfo en Hong Kong. Djokovic no derrotaba a tres top10 en el mismo evento desde las ATP Finals de Turín, en 2023. Alex de Miñaur se retiró lesionado a la altura del muslo de la pierna izquierda tras el primer juego del segundo set. El marcador murió con un 7-6(3) y 0-1. Novak ganó la manga inicial y tuvo que pedir la presencia del fisioterapeuta porque se dolía a la altura del abdomen. Le pasaban factura las dos batallas con Alexander Zverev y Daniil Medvedev. De Miñaur también pidió tratamiento por parte de otro fisio. En su caso se marchó a los vestuarios para que le vendaran el muslo de su pierna izquierda. Jugó un juego más y sacó la bandera blanca a la hora y 23 minutos. "Siento haberme tenido que retirar de esta manera. Toda mi admiración a Djokovic por lo que estás haciendo en el mundo del tenis", decía el tenista de Sidney en la ceremonia de premiación. "Hacía 11 años que no jugaba aquí. Sé que cuando me siento bien, puedo competir con cualquiera y esta semana ha sido una prueba de ello. Este título significa más de lo normal por todo lo que he tenido que pasar esta campaña", reflexionaba el vencedor, que se atrevió hablando en mandarín. El resultado de Djokovic en Pekín le permite superar a su víctima en la final y situarse noveno de la Race 2026. Hoy estaría dentro de la cita de maestros por la baja de Jannik Sinner. En el Masters 1000 de Shanghái, que se inicia este miércoles, el tenista de Belgrado espera al ganador del partido entre Hubert Hurkacz y James Duckworth.

articles.title: Coco Gauff decries racist abuse after halting play in win over Sun Xinran due to flickering LED lights
articles.summary: Coco Gauff said she has been sent an "insane" amount of racist comments following the play.
articles.body:
Coco Gauff is calling out racial abuse she's experienced following her win over Sun Xinran at the Beijing Open on Monday. During the match, Gauff halted play mid-point after LED lights next to the court flickered.

The sequence occurred with Gauff trailing 4-5 in the first set. In the middle of a rally — just after she returned the ball — Gauff noticed the advertisement on the LED screens that run alongside the court switched. She threw her hands up before Xinran returned the ball, which dropped in for a point.

Gauff asked for a video review, in which it was determined the point would be replayed. She won that point this time around and then would up winning nine of the next 10 games to close out Xinran. The 16-year-old Xinran was emotional on the court.

At the conclusion of the match, Gauff apologized to Xinran at the net.

Despite that, Gauff received racist abuse on social media for her actions. It reached a point where the tennis star decided to publicly respond, saying the amount of racist comments sent her way after the match were "insane."

Her full comment — which came in a response to an X post in which Gauff was called a racial slur — read:

"hey everyone, you can dislike me or disagree about what happened without being racist. the amount of racist comments/dms I've received in the last few hours is insane. Lastly, I'm not a cheater or a thief."

She then shared a full explanation of her actions and why she halted play in that moment. Gauff said she noticed the flickering board earlier in the rally and decided to halt play after she saw the lights flicker a second time. She explained that challenging a point is within the rules and she did nothing wrong by pushing for that point to go to a review.

Gauff said she apologized to Xinran at the net and added, "I did not like to see her so emotional."

Gauff has battled racist comments and abuse multiple times over her career. In 2025, she said online abuse was a "given" for women in the sport. In April, she called out racist comments she received following a loss at the Madrid Open.

With her win Monday, Gauff advanced to the Round of 16 at the Beijing Open. She'll take on Elise Mertens on Wednesday to try and make it into the quarterfinals.

articles.title: Novak Djokovic wins record seventh China Open, moves one ATP title behind Roger Federer

articles.body: Novak Djokovic moved within one title of Roger Federer’s career tally after winning a record seventh China Open crown on Tuesday, taking his ATP singles title count to 102.The sixth-seeded Serbian was handed the trophy after Australia’s Alex de Minaur retired with a groin injury during the final. It also marked the 39-year-old’s 21st consecutive year with at least one singles title, underlining the extraordinary longevity of his career.Djokovic now has 102 ATP titles, just one behind Federer’s 103 and seven behind Jimmy Connors’ Open Era record of 109.De Minaur had pushed Djokovic hard in the opening set, using aggressive groundstrokes and saving two break points. I want to say sorry to all the amazing fans,” De Minaur said during the trophy presentation.“I didn't want to finish like this... hopefully see you next year,” added the 27-year-old.Third straight top-10 win in BeijingDjokovic’s run to the title included three consecutive victories over top-10 opponents. He defeated US Open champion Alexander Zverev in the quarterfinals before advancing past Daniil Medvedev in the semifinals after the Russian was disqualified for hitting a spectator with a ball.De Minaur had reached the final after Hubert Hurkacz retired injured during their semifinal, but was chasing his first China Open title and a second trophy of the season following his Rotterdam triumph in February.For Djokovic, the Beijing triumph provides another landmark in a career that continues to add to its record book. articles.title: Novak Djokovic: Former world No 1 wins China Open title without needing a match point in semi-final and final
articles.summary: Novak Djokovic earns his seventh career title in Beijing after Alex De Minaur is forced to retire injured after Daniil Medvedev was defaulted in their semi-final; you can watch the WTA/ATP China Open and ATP 1000 Shanghai Masters live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Djokovic, who was awarded a win after his semi-final opponent Daniil Medvedev was disqualified after hitting a spectator with the ball , claimed the 102nd title of his career following the retirement of De Minaur in the final.

De Minaur, who left the ​court for ⁠a medical ⁠timeout after the first set, ‌continued playing with a heavy bandage on ‌his left thigh. But he could not continue after winning ⁠the first game ​of the second ​set.

Djokovic narrowly won ​the first set, ⁠with the match poised at ⁠7-6 (7-3) 0-1 when ​De Minaur retired.

"It's been 11 years since I last played here," Djokovic explained during the trophy ceremony. "I always have high expectations of myself and always want to visualise myself with the trophy, particularly here in Beijing, a place where I have never lost. But I was also aware that reality is a little bit different these days."

The 102nd tour-level title of Djokovic's career moves him within one of Roger Federer's 103 for second-most in the Open Era, behind only Jimmy Connors' 109.

The 39-year-old Serbian also extended his perfect record at the ATP 500 event to 34-0.

It has also significantly strengthened his hopes of returning to the Nitto ATP Finals this year.

The two had gone toe to toe in the first set, targeting the baseline to pressure each other.

De Minaur ⁠almost broke Djokovic in the fifth game but the Serbian ​saved the break point with a full-stretch backhand down ​the sideline.

The Australian held firm but the 27-year-old's error count increased ​during the tie-break to hand the first set to Djokovic.

An exhausted Djokovic ⁠also needed treatment during the break and the 39-year-old was surprised when De Minaur signalled the end of the match.

"This year has been quite challenging for me: Lots of physical and health issues" Djokovic said.

"I was just trying to find a good feeling on the court. I know that I'm feeling well and striking the ball well, I can compete at the highest level. This week has been evidence of that."

"I want to say sorry to all the amazing fans who came to watch this match," said De Minaur, who last retired from an official match in 2017 when he was a teenager. "I didn't want to finish like this, so I'm really sorry. To my team - those who are here and also back home - thank you. It's been a great week and I'm sure there's plenty more to come."

'We do not want to see matches end in retirement'

"It's just the anticlimactic nature of it," a shocked former British No 1 Johanna Konta told Sky Sports Tennis . "You don't have the release of emotions.

"Djokovic was the best player this week because you can only ask a player to deal with the challenges that are presented to them and he dealt with the challenges that were ahead of him and that's all there is to it.

"We do not want to see matches end in retirement and Djokovic himself probably wouldn't want that either. However, I'm sure he was pleased that he wasn't necessarily stretched to his physical limits but he will be pleased with the good things that he did do this week.

"I would have been less surprised had Novak Djokovic retired."

articles.title: Carlos Alcaraz overtakes one of Andy Murray’s career records after winning the Japan Open title
articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz has already returned to winning ways after claiming the title at the Japan Open in Tokyo. Shortly after coming back from a five-month...
articles.body:
Carlos Alcaraz has already returned to winning ways after claiming the title at the Japan Open in Tokyo.

Shortly after coming back from a five-month break because of a wrist injury, Alcaraz beat Jiri Lehecka 7-6(7-4), 6-4 to lift the trophy at the ATP 500 tournament. It represents his third title of the 2026 season, and the 27th title of his sensational career so far.

The success, which follows titles at the Australian Open and Doha this year, has also helped the Spaniard overtake a career record from tennis legend Andy Murray . In fact, he is now behind only the iconic Big Three in the list for the most ATP 500 titles claimed of all time after his Japan Open glory.

Carlos Alcaraz overtakes Andy Murray's ATP 500 titles record

Following his superb success at the Japan Open, Alcaraz now boasts 10 ATP 500 titles. That is one more than Scottish hero Murray. He does, however, remain behind Roger Federer (16), Rafael Nadal (15) and Novak Djokovic (14) in the all-time list. At the time of writing, Djokovic was battling Alex de Minaur in the final of the China Open, another ATP 500 tournament.

Given that Alcaraz is still only 23 years old, it is undoubtedly a list that he can rapidly climb in the very near future. Up next for the Spanish star, however, is the Shanghai Masters, an ATP 1000 tournament. The main draw gets underway on Wednesday, with second seed Alcaraz receiving a bye into the second round.

Carlos Alcaraz successfully defends sixth ATP title

Alcaraz can be extremely proud of another successful run in Tokyo, where he was out to defend his title. The ATP superstar has just done exactly that, and it represents the sixth time that he has defended a title in his glittering career, as per OptaAce. The Spaniard also achieved the feat at Barcelona (2022-23), Madrid (2022-23), Indian Wells (2023-24), Wimbledon (2023-24), and Roland Garros (2024-25).

He is, however, the first man to go back-to-back in Tokyo since Pete Sampras back in 1993-94. It's a truly phenomenal feat from Alcaraz, who has shown time and again that he has very little problem entering tournaments as the defending champion.

And the stunning statistics certainly don't end there. The iconic figure has now extended his record at ATP 500 level to 21-0, last losing in the 2025 Barcelona Open final to Holger Rune. He battled past Lehecka in Tokyo after 96 minutes, having previously beaten Alex Michelsen, Matteo Arnaldi, Denis Shapovalov and Jaume Munar.

articles.title: Djokovic wins China Open after de Minaur retires, Alcaraz wins Japan Open
articles.summary: Novac Djokovic won 102nd match of his career, while ATP 500 tournament victory was Carlos Alcaraz’s third of the year.
articles.body:
Novak Djokovic won the China Open after his opponent Alex de Minaur retired from the final with injury, while Spaniard Carlos Alcaraz retained his Japan Open crown to continue his resurgence after a lengthy wrist injury layoff.

The 39-year-old Serbian won the first set in the tie-break 7-6 (7-3) and was down a game in the second set when the Australian ended the match with retirement on Tuesday.

Djokovic extended an astonishing unbeaten streak in Beijing and winning the 102nd title of his career.

De Minaur left the court for a medical timeout after losing the first-set tie break but played on with his left thigh heavily bandaged. However, he had to stop after winning the first game of the second set, leaving him trailing 7-6(3) 0-1.

“I don’t feel great … I want to say sorry to all the amazing fans,” de Minaur said at the trophy presentation.

“I didn’t want to finish like this … hopefully see you next year,” added the 27-year-old fifth seed.

Alcaraz made another slow start before cruising past unseeded Czech Jiri Lehecka 7-6(4) 6-4 in the Japan Open final on Tuesday.

The ATP 500 tournament victory is Alcaraz’s third of the year after the Australian Open and Qatar Open, before the 23-year-old was sidelined by an injury for nearly five months and returned at the US Open in late August.

“I’m really happy to be able to lift a trophy again,” Alcaraz said. “It’s been a while and obviously it’s extra special after my injury and my comeback, in the second tournament that I’m playing.

“It was a really tough week and I didn’t play my best tennis and my best level but I did find good solutions and that’s what matters in the end.”

Alcaraz became the first man to go back-to-back in Tokyo since American Pete Sampras won the men’s title in both 1993 and 1994.

The world number three started shakily, dropping serve in the first game, but soon recovered and dialled up the intensity to break world number 19 Lehecka’s serve with a scorching backhand to level at 3-3.

More uncharacteristic errors from Alcaraz gave Lehecka hope in the tiebreak, but the Spaniard unleashed a sublime drop-shot en route to clinching the opening set to lay the platform for his 27th title overall.

The seven-time Grand Slam champion took control midway through the second set, breaking to claim a 4-3 lead before sealing victory by forcing an error on match point and then celebrating wildly with his team courtside.

Alcaraz said his triumph helped erase the doubts that he faced during his injury break.

“A lot of negative thoughts come to your mind,” Alcaraz added: “If you’re going to come back healthy, if you’re going to come back the same as you were before, if I will be able to hit the ball normally without pain. I trusted myself and it worked out.”

Alcaraz will return to action at the Shanghai Masters where he will take on Argentina’s Juan Manuel Cerundolo or a qualifier first. The main draw of the ATP 1000 event begins on Wednesday.

articles.body:
Amazon’s Prime Big Deal Day sale , which is essentially just an October version of Prime Day, is now live. I’m happy to report there are plenty of Nintendo deals in the bunch. Well, sort of.

We aren’t seeing too many discounts on first-party Nintendo games, which makes sense coming out of Nintendo’s surprisingly generous “Customer Appreciation” sale . Still, there are some sneaky Pokemon discounts in the mix, alongside plenty of new Switch 2 editions getting their first price drops of the year.

If you want to bulk up your physical Switch 2 library (who doesn’t love that box art ?), here's what we'd recommend grabbing in the sale.

Nintendo Switch 2 Games on Sale for Prime Big Deal Day

Starting from the top, we do in fact have a couple of first-party Nintendo games. The main one is $20 off the latest Pokemon release , Legends Z-A, which might not have the most expansive world, but still has plenty of “exciting Pokemon encounters, well-written characters, and amusing side quests” according to our review . We’re also seeing a hefty price cut on Nintendo’s latest sports release, Mario Tennis Fever .

Otherwise, the real winners of October Prime Day are JRPG fans.

Octopath Traveler, which popularized the HD-2D style, is seeing a $20 discount on its most recent release, Octopath Traveler 0 . The Adventures of Elliot: The Millennium Tales , a new Square Enix IP in a similar style, has also dropped to its lowest price yet . Dragon Quest fans can secure discounts on recent remakes of the first, second, and seventh games.

I guarantee you even the six-month wait until Revelation isn’t enough time to work through those beasts.

If you’re looking for a more real-time action, you can once again save $20 on Capcom’s newest IP, Pragmata .

Also on the Capcom front, Resident Evil Requiem has dropped to its lowest price since launch . The latest Resident Evil game brings back none other than Leon, pairing him alongside Grace Ashcroft to offer “two separate strains of survival horror.”

If you still haven’t gotten your hands on the new Nintendo console, you officially have a couple of options. You have the standalone console, which very recently went up in price by $50 . Or you can check out some special editions and bundles .

Switch 2 + Nintendo Switch Sports Resort Bundle

If you don’t mind waiting a couple of weeks, the Zelda edition Switch 2 is launching alongside the Ocarina of Time remake (still full-price, I’m sorry) on October 29. Or, if you’re incredibly passionate about Nintendo boxing, you can check out the new bundle with Switch Sports Resort launching on October 22.

articles.title: Daniil Medvedev: Defaulted for hitting a spectator with the ball but was it the right decision or should he have been able to play on?
articles.summary: 'Frustration I wouldn't necessarily say is conducive to clarity of mind' - Johanna Konta and Jonathan Overend both admit Daniil Medvedev was "unfortunate" to have been defaulted against Novak Djokovic; you can watch the ATP 1000 Shanghai Masters live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Medvedev was trailing Djokovic 7-5 5-3 and had lost a point when he hit the ball coming off the wall.

The spectator, who was ​sitting in the first row behind Medvedev, clutched his left eye and appeared to ‌be in pain as he walked out of the gallery, assisted by stadium staff.

Speaking to Sky Sports , Jonathan Overend said: "From the first camera angle we saw the ball leaving Medvedev's racket and weren't sure where it had gone, but I later saw a different angle filmed from the stands and it clearly went straight from the racket into the face of this spectator and so from the minute that was obvious, it was an instant default.

"It was absolutely the correct decision. The rulebook is very clear about that and it was unfortunate for Medvedev. We take him at face value when he says he didn't mean to do it, but it did leave his racket with force and it did strike the spectator.

"It appeared to me that umpire Mohamed Lahyani appeared initially to be uncertain about whether or not to default him but it was only when the supervisor got involved and further views were taken into account that it was clear that it did strike the spectator on the full and disqualification was the correct decision and clearly everyone on court felt that regrettably was the right course of action."

Overend described Medvedev as a "curious character" with the former US Open champion mimicking Djokovic being tired or injured on court which he felt "didn't feel appropriate" in such a match and such an opponent.

"For the disqualification to happen a few games later, it was out of character in the sense that I haven't seen him do that before but with Medvedev over the years you expect the unexpected and there is a certain volatility to him so maybe we shouldn't have been too surprised," he said.

'He wouldn't intentionally hit a spectator'

Johanna Konta also feels Medvedev was "unfortunate" to have been defaulted after watching numerous replays of the incident.

The former British No 1 said: "I can almost with certainty say he wouldn't intentionally hit a spectator with a ball. However, we have seen him do other things out of frustration from kicking the microphone, smashing rackets, and mouthing off.

"He's got quite a vocabulary on him, so it's not out of character for him to get frustrated but he obviously misjudged the angle of his racket, he misjudged the height of the backboard, he misjudged his whole surroundings.

"Frustration I wouldn't necessarily say is conducive to clarity of mind, so more than anything if you're feeling angry and frustrated, you won't necessarily be in control of your ability as if you weren't, so he wouldn't have intentionally done that."

Overend claims you have take Medvedev at "face value" with people believing he did not do it intentionally. When reviewing the footage, he said: "I don't think you're saying for certain that he's not doing that deliberately because he hits it at pace.

"He slices it but it is travelling at pace. He's intentionally coming right under the ball to stun it, but then he plays a really bad shot."

Konta said: "Medvedev was caught in between when you slice and you try and hit it back to you against just hitting it flat against the backboard, but I think he realises that the ball kid is there and I think if you're frustrated and you're thinking 'I can't hit the backboard because if it hits the ball kid I'm going to get defaulted' I wonder if he got caught in no-man's land and that's why it looks in between two shots because where he has hit it is right above the ball kid's head.

"I cannot see Medvedev doing it intentionally. I cannot imagine what that felt like in the pit of his stomach."

Do the ATP need to unify the criteria once and for all?

"Where tennis has to be careful here is making sure there isn't a grey area with regards to this rule," explained Overend.

"I think back to the Winston-Salem final of 2024 which was when Alex Michelsen launched a ball like Medvedev into the spectators, very, very close to the court, but then the umpire went over to the spectators to see whether anybody had been hit directly and because it didn't appear to hit anybody directly or injure them, Michelsen, who was absolutely convinced that he was going to get defaulted from that match was effectively let off and he was allowed to continue.

"That to me is a grey area because that is almost saying the severity of the impact dictates whether the player is disqualified or not.

"Tennis has got to be quite careful that if there is a rule in place here, which there is, it's enforced with consistency. In my opinion, launching a ball at pace, into spectators, is an instant disqualification and has to be for the safety of everyone. Players have been defaulted for less, let's put it this way!"

articles.title: El lujo asiático de Alcaraz en Shanghái que le ahorra 2 horas y 78 kilómetros de coche cada día
articles.standfirst: El murciano se aloja en el majestuoso Amanyangyun, de la cadena de hoteles Aman de la que Djokovic es imagen
articles.summary: El murciano se aloja en el majestuoso Amanyangyun, de la cadena de hoteles Aman de la que Djokovic es imagen
articles.body: El calendario tenístico se ha trasladado de Pekín y Tokio a Shanghái, la ciudad más poblada del país con 26 millones de habitantes. Y uno de los grandes problemas son los desplazamientos, que se hacen eternos. Un total de 38,9 kilómetros separan el centro de Shanghái del Qi Zhong Tennis Center donde se disputa la competición. Eso significa cada día dos horas y 78 kilómetros en el transporte oficial. Alcaraz se ahorra este largo trayecto. El murciano vive en Shanghái el lujo asiático en primera persona. Y es que se aloja en el Amanyangyun, bajo las paredes de edificios que pertenecen a las dinastías Ming y Qing, las dos últimas en China y que datan de hace más de 150 años. La distancia entre el resort y las pistas de tenis es de escasamente 1,3 kilómetros, que en coche son tres minutos. El hotel cuenta con 24 suites, 13 pabellones y 13 villas, construidas a partir de 26 antiguas casas que datan de las dinastías Ming y Qing. El campeón de siete grandes repite por tercera vez estancia junto a su equipo en el Aman, que tiene su propio bosque con más de 10.000 árboles, donde se inmortalizó en 2023 con una línea de complementos de Luis Vuitton, la marca francesa de la que es imagen. articles.title: Coco Gauff admits being drained by online racist abuse after shock defeat to Elise Mertens at China Open
articles.summary: Elise Mertens upsets Coco Gauff for the first time in the China Open fourth round with the American subsequently pulling out of the Wuhan Open, while Arthur Fery wins in Shanghai; you can watch the WTA China Open and ATP 1000 Shanghai Masters live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Mertens snapped her losing streak against Gauff to record her first win in six matches 6-3 6-3 to reach the quarter-finals in Beijing on Wednesday.

When trailing 6-3 4-1 to Mertens, Gauff told her box: "I have no energy. I'm trying, I have no energy. I can't see the ball, I feel like I'm going to pass out.

"I'm going to just try to finish the match."

In her clash against 16-year-old home player Sun Xinran on Tuesday, Gauff was serving to stay in the first set at 4-5 when Sun thought she had hit a winner, but the American had already raised her hand to stop the point as a light in the side panels around the court was flickering.

The chair umpire then ordered the point to be replayed.

Gauff took the next three points to hold for 5-5, and then dropped just one more game in the match.

Gauff, who has an excellent record in China, was asked by reporters in Beijing whether she had been affected by the abuse, and she said: "It has been kind of draining, I'm not going to lie. I just turn off my phone and move on. There's nothing you can do.

"I think today I was just a bit flat. I just didn't play well. I think I wasn't moving well. There were a lot of things I didn't do well."

The 22-year-old tried to explain the situation, saying on social media site X: "It was an unfortunate situation but it is out of my control.

"Xinran is incredible talent and player, I apologised for the situation at the end of the match and she completely understood."

Gauff then responded to a racist reply to her post by saying: "Hey everyone, you can dislike me or disagree about what happened without being racist.

"The amount of racist comments/dms I've received in the last few hours is insane.

"Lastly, I 'm not a cheater or a thief."

Gauff, the 2024 Beijing champion, delivered a flat performance, racking up 34 unforced errors in total as Mertens held on in impressive style, winning 10 of her last 11 service points and sealing victory with her second ace.

"She's an incredible player, of course. I knew it was going to be a very tough match," Mertens said.

"But I had motivation. My coach/boyfriend, it's his birthday tomorrow. So this win is dedicated to him and all the work we do."

Gauff will not defend her title in Wuhan

Gauff later withdrew from the Wuhan Masters 1000 due to fatigue, meaning she will not defend her title.

She said in a statement: "I'm disappointed to withdraw from Wuhan, especially as the defending champion. I always love playing there. After a long year, my body needs some time to rest and recover. I look forward to returning next year."

Gauff is expected to represent the United States in the Billie Jean King Cup in November. They face Hungary on November 21-22 in Delray Beach.

Earlier, Iga Swiatek broke Iva Jovic's serve twice in the last four games to beat the 18-year-old American 6-1 6-3.

Swiatek, a six-time Grand Slam champion who has struggled at times this year, will next play Mertens.

"For sure (today), I was using more of the chances that I got," said Swiatek, who has now won 126 of 128 WTA 1000 matches in which she won the first set.

"I was more proactive. Maybe changing the directions more instead of just being solid, more intense. When I needed that, I could play long rallies and be in defence, as well. Everything was working today.

"I feel like my game has improved," Swiatek said reflecting on her recent form. "Obviously sometimes playing the tournament is a bit tricky. Not everything is depending on you. I believe what I'm doing makes sense moving forward. That gives me the most confidence.

"For sure when you have great results on a match, it's always a good boost of confidence. But tennis is tough. You need to be ready for every match. Your previous results are not going to give you anything. I'm going to push no matter what and we'll see how it goes."

British No 1 Arthur Fery claimed a big scalp by defeating former Grand Slam champion Marin Cilic at the Shanghai Masters on Wednesday.

Fery, who reached the Wimbledon semi-finals in the summer, beat the former US Open champion 7-6 (7-2) 6-1 to set up a second-round clash against Karen Khachanov .

articles.title: China Open: Coco Gauff on 'draining few days' after online racist abuse
articles.summary: Coco Gauff says she had a "draining" few days after receiving racist abuse online before her fourth-round China Open exit.
articles.body:
Coco Gauff said she had a "draining" few days after receiving racist abuse online before her fourth-round China Open exit.

The American received an "insane" amount of racist comments and direct messages following an incident in her third-round win over 16-year-old Sun Xinran on Monday.

China's Sun thought she had hit a winner late in the first set, but Gauff raised her hand to halt play because of a flickering light in the side panels surrounding the court.

After a video review - which players are allowed to request - the point was replayed, with Gauff winning it and subsequently going on to clinch the match.

The 22-year-old posted a lengthy statement explaining what had happened and later condemned the racist abuse she received in response.

Gauff was beaten 6-3 6-3 in her next match against Elise Mertens on Wednesday.

Asked how she had felt over the past 36 hours, Gauff said: "It has been kind of draining, I'm not going to lie.

"I just turn off my phone and move on. I mean, there's nothing you can do."

A spokesperson for the Women's Tennis Association said it was appalled by the abuse. It said it was in contact with Gauff "to offer our full support".

A statement given to the news agency AFP said the governing body was "seeking action" against the abusive content.

Gauff, who won the title in Beijing in 2024, committed 34 unforced errors and eight double faults against Mertens.

"I was just a bit flat. That's the main thing," Gauff said.

"The level was there at some points, I just didn't sustain it the whole match."

Belgium's Mertens will play former world number one Iga Swiatek in the quarter-finals after the six-time major champion beat American teenager Iva Jovic 6-1 6-3.

Elsewhere, Britain's Arthur Fery beat Marin Cilic 7-6 (7-2) 6-1 in the Shanghai Masters first round.

Fery came back from a break down in the first set before dominating the former US Open champion in the second to claim his first ATP Tour win since August.

The 24-year-old will face Russia's 26th seed Karen Khachanov next.

Coco Gauff says online racist abuse has left her feeling exhausted as she lost to Elise Mertens in the China Open.

The world number four, a Black American, turned in an uncharacteristically listless performance in Beijing on Wednesday, double-faulting eight times as she went down 6-3, 6-3 to her Belgian opponent.

Gauff, 22, was playing a day after she called out the “insane” amount of abuse she had received on the internet following her win over Chinese teenager Sun Xinran in the previous round.

“It has been kind of draining. I’m not going to lie,” Gauff said of the impact of the online comments.

“But I just turn off my phone and move on. There’s nothing you can do.”

Asked about the match, she said: “I think I just didn’t play well. I think I wasn’t moving well.

“There were a lot of things I didn’t do well. I thought Elise played well on the bigger points.”

During her previous match in Beijing, against Sun, Gauff requested a video review over flickering LED lights on the stadium’s advertising hoardings.

The move prompted some boos from the crowd. The umpire agreed to have the point replayed, and Gauff went on to win 7-5, 6-1.

Early on Tuesday, Gauff wrote on X: “Hey everyone, you can dislike me or disagree about what happened without being racist.”

She was responding to a post that contained a racial slur.

“The amount of racist comments and messages I’ve received in the last few hours is insane,” she wrote.

Gauff also clarified that she challenged the point before Sun had returned the ball, when she noticed the lights flicker for a second time.

Asked about the incident, a spokesperson for the Women’s Tennis Association, the global governing body, said it was “appalled by the racial abuse directed at Coco Gauff” and that it was “in contact with her to offer our full support”.

It added in a statement to the AFP news agency that there was “no place for racism, discrimination, or abuse in tennis”, and that it was “seeking action” against the abusive content.

Gauff, who won the Beijing title in 2024 and made the semifinals last year, was popular among fans during the tournament.

A group of supporters in the largely empty stadium tried to encourage her into a comeback on Wednesday.

Mertens was undeterred as she punched her ticket for a quarterfinal clash against Iga Swiatek.

The world number 19 called Gauff an “incredible player”, adding: “I knew it was going to be a very tough match.”

She dedicated her win to her coach, who is also her boyfriend.

Earlier, Swiatek swept aside American teenager Iva Jovic 6-1, 6-3 in one hour and 35 minutes.

“I had it under control from the beginning,” said the Polish world number nine. “I feel like I’m improving every day.”

articles.summary: Explore how Roger Federer and Serena Williams transformed their tennis success into massive business empires, leveraging partnerships, investments, and innovative ventures to create lasting financial legacies beyond the court.
articles.body: Roger Federer and Serena Williams did more than dominate their respective eras of the game of tennis. Their records brought them global recognition, which eventually became a foundation of businesses, investments and long-term commercial partnerships. Federer wrapped up his career with 20 Grand Slam singles titles, and Williams won 23, but their financial narratives increasingly extended beyond prize money.The difference is especially apparent in how each legend approached business after becoming a sporting icon. Federer has aligned himself with luxury brands and On, while Williams has built an investment-heavy portfolio through Serena Ventures and interests in beauty, media and sports. Celebrity Net Worth has their estimated fortunes to be substantial, but exact private-wealth figures can vary across sources.Roger Federer and Serena Williams built business empires that rival their extraordinary tennis fortunes off courtFederer's financial strategy has been heavily shaped by premium sponsorships and equity ownership. Forbes estimates that he earned more than $130 million in ATP Tour prize money during his career, while his commercial earnings became an even larger part of his wealth.His most notable business move came through On. Federer became involved with the Swiss athletic brand as a co-owner and creative partner, turning what could have been another traditional endorsement arrangement into an equity position, and Forbes estimated his stake at roughly 2.5% in August 2026, after On's share-price movements had a significant impact on his wealth.His commercial portfolio has also included long-running relationships with Rolex, Mercedes-Benz and Uniqlo. Rolex has worked with Federer since 2001, reinforcing the luxury positioning that has become central to his post-tennis brand.Serena Williams turned influence into investmentsWilliams followed a different route, moving aggressively into venture capital and entrepreneurship. She founded Serena Ventures in 2017, building an investment platform focused on early-stage businesses and founders who have historically received less access to capital. The firm raised $111 million for its inaugural fund and has invested in more than 60 brands, according to The New York Times.Her business interests extend beyond venture capital. Williams has developed Wyn Beauty, launched Nine Two Six Productions and maintained stakes in sports businesses, including the Miami Dolphins. Forbes also identifies Serena Ventures as a major part of her ongoing investment activity.According to Celebrity Net Worth, Serena Williams' estimated net worth is also in the hundreds of millions. Their championship records provided credibility, worldwide visibility and commercial leverage that could be transferred into businesses.Federer used that leverage to secure long-term partnerships and ownership opportunities, and his On investment demonstrated the potential difference between receiving a fixed endorsement fee and owning part of a rapidly growing company, also, his continued relationship with Rolex also illustrates how his reputation remains commercially valuable years after retirement.Williams, meanwhile, transformed her influence into an investment platform. Serena Ventures describes its mission around backing founders reshaping how people live, work, move and connect, with Serena Williams serving as managing partner.Roger Federer’s estimated $1.1 billion net worth places him well ahead of Serena Williams, whose fortune is estimated at roughly $300 million to $400 million. Federer’s wealth has been driven heavily by major endorsement partnerships and his reported stake in Swiss sportswear company On, while Williams has built significant wealth through endorsements, including Nike, and her venture capital firm Serena Ventures. Their comparison highlights how both converted elite tennis careers into substantial business and investment portfolios beyond prize money.Their financial legacies therefore extend well beyond tennis statistics. articles.title: Adolfo Daniel Vallejo Flew Alone to Florida at 12. Now He Carries Paraguayan Tennis Worldwide
articles.summary: A new name emerged in this week's career high ATP ranking list, Paraguay's Adolfo Daniel Vallejo. Vallejo, now #56 in the world, posted a historic result for...
articles.body:
A new name emerged in this week's career high ATP ranking list, Paraguay's Adolfo Daniel Vallejo.

Vallejo, now #56 in the world, posted a historic result for his country in ATP Tokyo, becoming the first man from Paraguay to reach the quarterfinals of a 500 level event. Like most things in his career, the 22-year-old Vallejo, did it the hard way, and it all began with a plane ride to Florida when he was 12.

Adolfo Daniel Vallejo's Historic Week in Tokyo

The ATP Tokyo qualifying field was loaded, and Vallejo had to navigate it, defeating home hero Taro Daniel, and Jaime Faria from Portugal to reach the main draw. The win over Faria was in three sets.

Upon entering the main draw, Vallejo upset the #4 seed Rafael Jodar in a battle of u-23 talents, dismantling the Spaniard who has generated significant attention on the ATP Tour this season 6-1 6-3. A straight set win over Matteo Berrettini followed, before Vallejo had a poor outing against Jiri Lehecka in the quarterfinals, Lehecka went on to reach the final.

The result pushed his ranking firmly into the top 60, and sets him up for a first round match in Shanghai against Valentin Royer.

Adolfo Daniel Vallejo was an unknown at the ATP level until 2026, having previously featured on the ATP Challenger Tour dating back to 2023 when he was a teenager. Vallejo continued to mix ATP Challenger and ATP Tour level matches in 2026, but he's clearly graduated from the Challenger Tour with a 22-5 record at that level this season. Vallejo reached two Challenger finals on Clay, and won two more Challengers, consecutively, in January.

On the main tour, he's put together a solid 14-15 campaign and is expanding his game beyond the clay court base that many South American players are raised on.

Vallejo has been able to debut in three of the four Grand Slams in 2026, and won a match at Roland Garros against Cameron Norrie. Beyond the Grand Slams, Vallejo qualified for Madrid and beat Grigor Dimitrov, in Bastad he slipped into the semifinals, he also notched a win over Valentin Vacherot on the hard courts of Cincinnati.

While Vallejo has yet to secure that headline grabbing top 10 win, the trend line is such that's established himself on clay, and is now moving beyond that to become an all-court player.

Vallejo is not an unknown for those who follow junior tennis, he began to show his talent at a young age, after that plane ride to play in the Orange Bowl at 12, At 14, he joined the IMG Academy in Florida on scholarship. Vallejo is the fourth player from Paraguay in the ATP top 100, and is primed for success. The last successful pro player from Paraguay? His mentor Ramon Delgado.

He was world Junior #1 in 2022, and won the Orange Bowl at 17, he's also spent time at the Nadal Academy back in 2023. In March, Vallejo told ATPTour.com "You're also fighting against what everyone thinks you should do. The mentality [in Paraguay] is not to go pro"

The piece also touched on the barriers players from countries that are not traditional powers face, Vallejo rarely received direct wild cards to bigger tournaments to enhance his ranking, and he never got to play on home soil, while even players from Argentina, Chile, and Brazil get that opportunity in South America.

Alongside Peru's Ignacio Buse , Vallejo is part of a new generation of talent from South America that are not household names yet.

No wild cards, no shortcuts, just the long way up has been Adolfo Daniel Vallejo's path to a near top 50 ranking on the ATP Tour. He has the talent and the form to make noise at the ATP Shanghai Masters, and is worth watching as the 2026 season heads to a conclusion. His performance in Tokyo showed his game can also be competitive on hard courts. Watch him tonight against Valentin Royer, and in the weeks to come as he keeps fine tuning his game, and trying to fulfill his tremendous promise as a junior.

articles.title: Greg Rusedski names his favourite for the ATP Finals between Carlos Alcaraz, Alexander Zverev and Novak Djokovic
articles.summary: The two-time defending ATP Finals champion, Jannik Sinner, won’t compete in Turin this year. Earlier this week, Sinner ended his season early due to injury.....
articles.body:
The two-time defending ATP Finals champion, Jannik Sinner, won't compete in Turin this year.

Earlier this week, Sinner ended his season early due to injury . Carlos Alcaraz, Alexander Zverev, and Novak Djokovic are arguably the three players most likely to take the title in his absence.

But who is the favourite? Former Grand Slam finalist Greg Rusedski has now picked his ATP Finals winner from the three players listed above.

Greg Rusedski picks Carlos Alcaraz as his favourite to win the 2026 ATP Finals

"I say Carlos [Alcaraz], and I say Novak Djokovic is the danger man. Let's not forget, [Alexander] Zverev has won it on two occasions, so it's going to be a battle of those three guys. But if I had to pick one guy right now, I think Carlos is building nicely; he's still not at his best, but he's winning," he said during the latest episode of ' Off Court with Greg Rusedski '.

Djokovic is a record seven-time ATP Finals champion, and Zverev has also won multiple titles, lifting the trophy in 2018 and 2021. Alcaraz, on the other hand, has never won the year-end championships, but that didn't stop Rusedski from picking him as his winner.

Rusedski did, however, admit that Alcaraz isn't at 'his best' and explained that in more detail, referencing his serve, which he believes was better earlier this year at the Australian Open.

"It's the foot movement as well as the toss being lower. I think he had the perfect balance in Australia; it was more accurate, a little bit more similar to Novak Djokovic. He's trying to get that toss lower. When you get a lower toss, you get more disguise; you also get a little bit more pop, but it's harder to time," he said.

"I feel his rhythm isn't quite there with the toss and the footwork; he's trying things out. It's going to come down to Sammy Lopez and Carlos, what they feel is best. At the moment, I just don't see him serving quite as well and as accurately as he was at the start of the year; it might be his wrist as well – we don't know. We're not a part of the team."

Alcaraz only recently returned to tennis at the US Open, having spent several months sidelined with a wrist injury. He didn't win the title in New York, but won the Laver Cup and the Japan Open shortly after, re-emerging as a frontrunner for the ATP Finals.

Rusedski thinks Alcaraz, Djokovic, and Zverev will 'battle' for the ATP Finals crown; however, they won't be the only players in Turin. As things stand, here are the eight players set to compete for the title.

2026 ATP Finals qualifiers (as it stands)

Greg Rusedski says Jannik Sinner will leave no stone unturned in his recovery from injury

Eight men will fight for the ATP Finals title this November, but Sinner won't be one of them. The two-time defending champion will skip his home tournament with a knee injury. Rusedski shared his thoughts on Sinner's withdrawal from the ATP Finals and his decision to end his 2026 campaign early.

He's probably taking the cautious route, trying to do it without surgery. When you can avoid surgery, it's always better not to have it. If he had no choice, he would have had surgery by now and been recuperating, so he's trying to avoid that," he said.

"It will be interesting to see what the problem is, whether it's a meniscus or a patella problem, where the injury in the knee is exactly, and finding a solution. He won't leave any stone unturned. We heard the rumours that he might not be playing for the rest of the season; this is confirmed, and that means we're going to have a new world number one guaranteed, most likely Sascha Zverev."

articles.summary: Estará junto a Sinner, Gauff y Osaka en el El 'Million Dollar 1 Point Slam, que mide a 10 jugadores aficionados de toda Australia contra 22 profesionales
articles.body: El próximo 13 de enero de 2027, el plato fuerte de la semana previa del Open de Australia será la segunda edición del 'Million Dollar 1 Point Slam', que mide a 10 jugadores aficionados de toda Australia contra 22 profesionales. La organización del primer grande ya ha confirmado la presencia de Carlos Alcaraz, Jannik Sinner, Coco Gauff y Naomi Osaka. El ganador se llevará un millón de dólares australianos a a casa. Los partidos serán a un solo punto. Se utiliza el 'piedra, papel o tijera' para determinar quién sacará o recibirá, y el ganador del punto pasa a la siguiente ronda. La fase clasificatoria se celebrará a lo largo de la geografía australiana mientras que el cuadro final ya será en las dependencias del Melbourne Park. La final se disputará en la Rod Laver Arena, la pista principal del complejo tenístico. La primera edición la ganó Jordan Smith, un profesor de tenis afincado en Sidney. Él fue quien se llevó el millón de dólares australianos, que al cambio corresponden a 621.511 euros. Jordan logró el billete al torneo tras quedar campeón del estado de Nueva Gales del Sur. Trabaja habitualmente tirando bolas en la Castle Hill Tennis Academy, donde lleva la escuela del club junto a sus padres Neil y Michelle. El torneo instalará la grada temporal más grande jamás construida en Melbourne Park, al triplicar las zonas de sombra y aumentar en un 45 % el espacio en una renovada Grand Slam Oval. Cabe recordar que el cuadro principal del Open de Australia se iniciará el domingo 17 de enero y se alargará hasta el lunes 31.

articles.title: Ferrero desvela su "batalla perdida" con Alcaraz y no descarta entrenar a Sinner: "Dicen que no sería ético..."
articles.standfirst: Juan Carlos Ferrero piensa en volver al circuito ATP y no descarta entrenar a Rafa Jódar o Jannik Sinner
articles.summary: Juan Carlos Ferrero piensa en volver al circuito ATP y no descarta entrenar a Rafa Jódar o Jannik Sinner
articles.body: Juan Carlos Ferrero, antiguo entrenador de Carlos Alcaraz, desveló el 15 de septiembre que volvería al circuito ATP como el año que viene. El extenista, que está presentando su libro 'Mentalidad Ganadora', confiesa en una entrevista concedida al programa 'El Larguero' que "está naciendo en mí ese instinto de volver a la competición" y reconoció que los motivos de su ruptura con Carlos Alcaraz "darían posiblemente para otro libro". "Mi ruptura con Alcaraz son cosas personales, no hay que decir a los cuatro vientos lo que pasa interiormente. Entre la familia y yo hubo aspectos en los que no nos pusimos de acuerdo y ya está, no pasa nada... ¿Si la ruptura daría para otro libro? Supongo que sí. Hay historias buenas, malas, regulares... habría mucho que contar. Alcaraz me tiene enamorado viéndolo por televisión y lo disfruto jugando", le contó a Manu Carreño. Juan Carlos Ferrero compartió que "en lo que más trabajé con Carlos Alcaraz fue en controlarse a sí mismo... Es tan perfeccionista que se flagelaba mucho". El exjugador habla de "los peligros" en torno Alcaraz y "las compañías, las amistades peligrosas, le advertía al igual que su familia quién es su amigo y quién iba por interés. Ojo a la noche, descansa bien... Le decía que no mirase las redes sociales... una batalla perdida. Peleé mucho por eso. Perdí la batalla... no fueron pocas". Juan Carlos Ferrero sigue sin desvelar el nombre del jugador al que podría entrenar, "no tengo absolutamente nada cerrado con nadie y en estos dos meses, de aquí a diciembre, habrá movimientos", pero habló sobre los nombres que más suenan en estos momentos, los de Rafa Jódar y Jannik Sinner. "¿Si me gustaría entrenar a Rafa Jodar? No me cierro la puerta. Tiene muchísimo potencial, tiene muchas ganas, joven, que quiere comerse el mundo y si viene la oferta, la estudiaré", reconoció. Preguntado por la posibilidad de entrenar a Jannik Sinner contestó que "quiero seguir creciendo en mi carrera deportiva como entrenador y no me puedo cerrar la puerta de Jannik". "He escuchado a gente diciendo que no es ético y que cómo puedo entrenar al rival de Carlos Alcaraz, pero toda esa gente no piensa en mí. Quiero crecer como entrenador y cerrarme la puerta a un jugador como Jannik sería de tontos", subrayó. Ferrero desveló que "he tenido propuestas buenas, sobre todo a principio de año, pero no estaba preparado" y destacó que "ahora ha llegado el momento". "No se puede saber si de Sinner o no. Me encantaría ponerme en posición de entrenar a un tenista con posibilidades de ganar cosas", apuntó.

articles.title: Alcaraz, ambicioso: "Quiero ganar en Shanghái y los torneos que vienen al menos una vez"
articles.standfirst: Al murciano le falta el Masters 1000 chino, el de París, las ATP Finals y la Copa Davis
articles.summary: Al murciano le falta el Masters 1000 chino, el de París, las ATP Finals y la Copa Davis
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz, a sus 23 años, afronta lo que resta de temporada con una frescura que no había tenido en los años precedentes. Y todo por la lesión en la muñeca derecha que le tuvo sin competir cuatro meses y medio. El murciano, campeón el martes del Open 500 de Tokio, ambiciona ahora ganar Shanghái, uno de los tres Masters 1000 que faltan en su palmarés junto a Canadá y París. "Ahora mismo, solo quiero estar en buenas condiciones para este torneo, porque realmente quiero ganar tanto este como los que tengo dentro de un par de meses al menos una vez", reflexiona. "Me siento fresco mentalmente y eso es lo más importante". Tras Shanghái y el Six Kings Slam y París, en el calendario del tenista de El Palmar aparecen las ATP Finals de Turín (15 al 22 de noviembre) y la fase final de la Copa Davis (24 al 29), los dos eventos más importantes que aún no están en su palmarés. "Doy gracias por ser español. Representar a mi bandera es una de las mejores cosas que me pueden pasar", indica. La ausencia del lesionado Jannik Sinner convierte a Carlitos y a España en favoritos, con el permiso de Alexander Zverev.
